args.message:
Fix FIN-212: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for banker's rounding in money.py

The round_money() docstring claimed banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN,
per FIN-212) but the implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP, causing
tests/test_money.py to fail (2.665 rounded to 2.67 instead of 2.66).

Replace ROUND_HALF_UP with ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix FIN-212: implement banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money()
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming otherwise. For example, `2.665` rounded to `2.67` instead of the expected `2.66`.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: replaced `ROUND_HALF_UP` with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money()` so the implementation matches the documented FIN-212 behavior.

## Testing
- Ran CI on branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` (run `ci-0001`, commit `08d3cd5986`): **passed**, including `tests/test_money.py`.

@alex — this is a behavior-correct change for a payments rounding rule, so I'd appreciate your review. I will not merge until approved.
